checklist.step: Open the release-gate record when a product enters the launch pipeline
actions: In the product governance workflow tool create a new release-gate record and link it to the product's business case.
Enter product name, line of business (Life or Personal Lines), target launch date, and whether it is a new product or a material change to an existing one.
Ask the Product / Filing Actuary and Product Development for the target market statement draft and the distribution strategy note.
Set the record status to 'Awaiting POC pack' and notify the Product Oversight Committee secretariat.
checklist.done: the release-gate record exists with product, line of business, target date and an 'Awaiting POC pack' status.

checklist.step: Assemble the target market statement and distribution strategy
actions: Draft the target market statement covering customer type, needs and objectives, and characteristics the product is NOT designed for (negative target market).
Document the intended distribution channels and any restrictions needed to keep the product reaching only its target market.
Ask the Distribution Specialist to confirm the proposed channels can apply the stated restrictions.
Attach both documents to the release-gate record.
checklist.done: a target market statement and distribution strategy, confirmed feasible by Distribution, are attached to the record.

checklist.step: Commission the fair value / Consumer Duty outcomes assessment
actions: Build the value assessment: price, cost of manufacture and distribution, expected claims/benefit ratio, and comparison against similar products in the market.
Score the product against the four Consumer Duty outcomes (products & services, price & value, consumer understanding, consumer support).
Flag any outcome scoring below the internal threshold to the Insurance Product Manager for redesign before the pack is submitted.
Attach the completed value assessment to the release-gate record.
checklist.done: a value assessment covering all four Consumer Duty outcomes is attached, with any below-threshold outcome remediated or explicitly accepted.

checklist.step: Compile and run the required product testing
actions: Run readability testing on all customer-facing documents (policy summary, IPID, terms) against the plain-language standard.
Run distribution-channel testing to confirm sales scripts and point-of-sale material match the stated target market.
Capture screenshots or recordings of the tested journeys and the readability score report.
Attach the test evidence pack to the release-gate record.
checklist.done: readability and distribution testing evidence is attached and any failed test is remediated before submission.

checklist.step: Submit the complete pack to the Product Oversight Committee
actions: Check the release-gate record has: target market statement, distribution strategy, value assessment, test evidence, and a proposed launch date.
Submit the pack to the POC secretariat at least 10 business days ahead of the next scheduled sitting.
Present the pack at the POC meeting and answer questions on target market, value and testing.
Record the POC decision (approved / approved with conditions / rejected) and the sitting date on the release-gate record.
checklist.done: the pack is submitted, presented, and a dated POC decision is recorded on the release-gate record.

checklist.step: Clear any conditions the POC attached to its approval
actions: List every condition from the POC minutes as its own line item with an owner and a due date.
Chase each owner and collect the closing evidence (revised wording, updated training, fixed system field).
Route closing evidence back to the POC secretariat for confirmation the condition is satisfied.
Update the release-gate record status to 'Conditions cleared' once every line item is closed.
checklist.done: every POC condition has closing evidence confirmed by the secretariat and the record shows 'Conditions cleared'.

checklist.step: Set the release flag in the build environment to blocked by default
actions: In the Policy Administration Platform open the product build for the target product and set the go-live/release flag to 'Blocked — awaiting governance sign-off'.
Confirm no rating or quote configuration for the product can be activated to new business while the flag is blocked.
Record the flag status and the field name/screen used in the release-gate record.
Notify the Insurance Product Manager the technical block is in place.
checklist.done: the build environment shows the product go-live flag blocked, confirmed by a named field/screen reference.

checklist.step: Confirm any statutory or regulator review period has fully run
actions: Check whether the product or any linked notification (e.g. a new-product notification) carries a review or objection period under the FCA rules or a related filing.
Where a period applies, compute the earliest permitted go-live date and compare it to the target launch date.
Where the target date is unreachable, notify the Insurance Product Manager and Compliance Officer immediately.
Record the computed earliest go-live date on the release-gate record.
checklist.done: the record shows either 'no review period applies' or a computed earliest go-live date that the launch respects.

checklist.step: Release the product only after POC sign-off is dated on the record
actions: Confirm the release-gate record shows 'Conditions cleared' and a dated POC approval that pre-dates today.
In the Policy Administration Platform change the release flag from 'Blocked' to 'Live' and record the change timestamp.
Screenshot the flag change and attach it to the release-gate record as the release evidence.
Notify Distribution and the contact centre that the product is live for new business.
checklist.done: the release flag is changed to Live only after a dated POC sign-off, with a timestamped screenshot on file.

checklist.step: Publish the product governance file to the compliance evidence repository
actions: Copy the completed release-gate record — pack, POC minutes, conditions log, flag-change evidence — into the compliance evidence repository under the product name and launch date.
Apply the 6-year retention label running from expected product withdrawal.
Confirm the repository entry is indexed and searchable by product name and POC sitting date.
checklist.done: the governance file is filed, labelled for retention, and searchable by product name.

checklist.step: Track the product through its post-launch review point
actions: Diarise a post-launch review at the interval set by the POC (typically 12 months or sooner for higher-risk products).
At the review, pull actual sales, complaints and claims data against the target market and value assessment.
Flag any drift from the intended target market to the POC for a fresh governance decision.
checklist.done: a post-launch review is diarised and, once due, completed with a documented outcome.

checklist.step: Log any launch that slipped past its target date and record the cause
actions: Where the actual go-live date is later than the original target, record the delay reason (POC rework, testing fail, review period) on the release-gate record.
Assess whether the delay caused any interim mis-selling exposure (e.g. sales staff already briefed on the old date).
Notify the Compliance Officer of any exposure found.
checklist.done: delayed launches carry a recorded cause and a documented exposure assessment.

checklist.step: Escalate any pressure to release before sign-off
actions: Where a business owner requests bypassing the release flag ahead of POC sign-off, log the request on the release-gate record.
Escalate to the Head of Compliance the same business day; the flag is never manually overridden without documented Head of Compliance approval.
Record the final decision and its rationale on the record.
checklist.done: every bypass request is logged, escalated and closed with a recorded, approved decision — never a silent override.

checklist.step: Reconcile the product launch calendar to the release-gate log monthly
actions: Pull the product launch calendar and match every entry to a release-gate record.
Flag any launch calendar entry with no matching release-gate record as a control gap.
Route control gaps to the Insurance Product Manager for immediate remediation.
checklist.done: every calendar launch has a matching release-gate record, with gaps remediated the same month.

checklist.step: Report release-gate status to the Product Oversight Committee each sitting
actions: Prepare a status pack listing products released, pending and blocked, with days-to-target for each pending item.
Present the pack at the POC's standing governance item.
Record any committee direction (e.g. escalation, resourcing) in the minutes and action log.
checklist.done: a release-gate status pack is presented at every POC sitting with directions captured in the minutes.

testing.step: Build the population of products released in the period
actions: Extract from the Policy Administration Platform every product build with a go-live/release flag change to 'Live' inside the test period.
Add any product notified to distribution partners as available for sale even without a formal build change.
Reconcile the extract to the product launch calendar and resolve any count difference before sampling.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to the launch calendar and signed as complete.

testing.step: Match every released product to a dated POC sign-off
actions: Match each population row to its release-gate record and POC sign-off date.
Compare the sign-off date to the release-flag change timestamp.
List any row with no matching sign-off, or a sign-off dated after go-live, as an automatic exception.
testing.done: every population row is matched to a pre-dated sign-off or listed as an exception.

testing.step: Select and document the test sample
actions: Take 100% of products flagged higher-risk by the POC risk rating.
Take a further random sample covering at least 25% of the remaining population, minimum 10 products.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and covers all higher-risk products.

testing.step: Re-perform the target market and value assessment review for sampled products
actions: Read the target market statement and value assessment for each sampled product independently of the original sign-off.
Reach an independent view on whether the product design supports the stated target market and the four Consumer Duty outcomes.
Log any disagreement with the original POC conclusion as an exception.
testing.done: each sampled product has an independent re-performance note, with disagreements logged as exceptions.

testing.step: Trace the release-flag change to the timestamped system evidence
actions: In the Policy Administration Platform pull the audit log for the release flag on each sampled product.
Confirm the flag change timestamp, the user who made it, and that it moved from Blocked to Live only once sign-off existed.
Capture the audit log extract into the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled product's flag-change audit log is captured and confirms the block was lifted only after sign-off.

testing.step: Check every POC condition on the sample was genuinely closed before go-live
actions: Pull the conditions log for each sampled product with conditional approval.
Confirm closing evidence exists for every condition and pre-dates the go-live timestamp.
Flag any condition closed after go-live, or with no closing evidence, as an exception.
testing.done: every conditional approval in the sample has fully closed, pre-dated evidence, or is logged as an exception.

testing.step: Recompute any regulator review period on the sample
actions: For sampled products carrying a review or objection period, recompute the earliest permitted go-live date.
Compare to the actual go-live timestamp and flag any product launched before the period lapsed.
Treat an early launch as a reportable breach, not a documentation exception.
testing.done: no sampled product launched before its review period lapsed, or the breach is escalated.

testing.step: Verify post-launch reviews are diarised and, where due, completed
actions: Check each sampled product has a diarised post-launch review date.
Where the review date has passed, confirm the review was completed with documented findings.
Log missing or overdue reviews as exceptions.
testing.done: every sampled product's post-launch review is diarised and, if due, evidenced as completed.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with product name, what was missed and the customer impact.
Assign a root cause and an owner, and set a remediation date.
For any product used before sign-off, open a self-assessment with Regulatory Counsel on customer remediation.
Carry open exceptions into the next quarter's test as mandatory retest rows.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance threshold.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) referencing the evidence.
Have the independent reviewer, who sat on none of the sampled POC sessions, sign the workpaper.
Report results to the Product Oversight Committee and file the workpaper in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and exception rate is filed and reported to the POC.

checklist.step: Open a configuration build ticket from the approved product change
actions: Open a build ticket in the change management tool linked to the release-gate record and the POC approval reference.
Attach the approved wording, rate tables and rule set exactly as signed off by the POC.
Set the ticket target date to the product's approved go-live date less UAT lead time.
Assign the ticket to a Configuration Engineer.
checklist.done: the ticket exists, links to the approval reference, and carries the approved source documents.

checklist.step: Configure the approved wording and product structure in the policy admin system
actions: In the policy admin system open the product model builder and create or amend the product version.
Enter form numbers, edition dates and clause wording fields exactly matching the approved source document.
Set effective and expiry dates on each wording version so no in-force policy is unintentionally re-worded.
Save as a draft version pending review.
checklist.done: the draft product version's wording fields match the approved source document field-for-field.

checklist.step: Configure the approved rates and rules in the rating engine
actions: In Earnix open the rating model for the product and enter base rates, factors and territory relativities from the approved rate exhibit.
Enter eligibility and underwriting rules from the approved rule set into the rules engine module.
Version-control the change with the approval reference number as the version label.
Save as draft pending review.
checklist.done: the draft rating model's rates and rules match the approved rate exhibit and rule set.

checklist.step: Run a field-by-field comparison against the approved source
actions: Export the draft configuration (wording fields, rate tables, rules) from the policy admin and rating systems.
Compare it line by line against the approved source documents attached to the build ticket.
Log every discrepancy on the ticket with the field name and both values.
Return the ticket to the Configuration Engineer for correction of any discrepancy.
checklist.done: a documented field-by-field comparison exists with zero open discrepancies before proceeding.

checklist.step: Peer review the configuration for logic and downstream impact
actions: Review the configuration change for correct rule sequencing, dependency on other in-force products, and quote-engine calculation logic.
Check the change does not alter rating or wording for any other live product sharing the same shared rule tables.
Approve the peer review on the ticket or return it with named required fixes.
checklist.done: a peer reviewer distinct from the builder has approved the change with no open findings.

checklist.step: Execute user acceptance testing against approved scenarios
actions: Build UAT test cases covering standard risks, edge-case risks, and at least one scenario per rating factor tier.
Run the test cases in the UAT environment and record actual premium/wording output against the expected output from the approved rate exhibit.
Log any output mismatch as a defect and return to the Configuration Engineer.
Attach the signed-off UAT report to the ticket.
checklist.done: a UAT report with zero open defects is attached to the ticket.

checklist.step: Obtain business sign-off from the product owner before deployment
actions: Review the UAT report and the field comparison summary.
Confirm the configuration matches the product approved at POC and no unapproved scope crept in.
Sign the ticket approving deployment to production.
Where anything does not match, block deployment and route back to Configuration Engineer.
checklist.done: the product owner's dated sign-off is on the ticket before any production deployment is scheduled.

checklist.step: Deploy the configuration to production under change control
actions: Raise a change request in the change management tool referencing the build ticket and required approvals.
Deploy the configuration in the scheduled release window and capture the deployment log with timestamp and deployer identity.
Verify in production that the effective date matches the approved go-live date, not before.
Close the change request with the deployment log attached.
checklist.done: the deployment log shows the correct effective date, deployer identity, and is attached to a closed change request.

checklist.step: Run a post-deployment smoke test in production
actions: Quote a small set of the UAT scenarios in the live production environment.
Compare the production output to the UAT expected output.
Log and escalate immediately any mismatch found in production.
checklist.done: production smoke-test output matches UAT expected output for every scenario run.

checklist.step: Record the system change on the release-gate and compliance record
actions: Attach the closed ticket, comparison log, UAT report and deployment log to the release-gate record.
Copy the full evidence set to the compliance evidence repository under the product and effective date.
Apply the 6-year retention label.
checklist.done: the system change record is filed and retention-labelled, cross-referenced to the release-gate record.

checklist.step: Reconcile in-force policy wording to the deployed version monthly
actions: Pull a sample of policies issued after the deployment date and check the wording version and rate applied.
Compare to the version that should apply given the policy's issue date.
Escalate any mismatch to the Policy Admin Ops Lead immediately.
checklist.done: sampled post-deployment policies show the correct wording and rate version for their issue date.

checklist.step: Restrict production configuration access to authorised roles
actions: Review the access list for the policy admin and rating system production configuration modules quarterly.
Confirm only Configuration Engineers and Release Engineers with an open, approved change ticket can deploy to production.
Remove or flag any access held outside that population.
checklist.done: production configuration access is limited to the authorised population, confirmed quarterly.

checklist.step: Track outstanding configuration tickets against the go-live calendar
actions: Pull open configuration tickets weekly and compare target dates to the product go-live calendar.
Escalate any ticket at risk of missing its go-live date to the Insurance Product Manager.
Record the escalation and resulting decision on the ticket.
checklist.done: at-risk tickets are escalated weekly with a recorded decision before the go-live date is missed.

checklist.step: Log any emergency or out-of-cycle configuration change separately
actions: Where a change bypasses the standard release window (production incident fix, urgent rate correction), open an emergency change ticket.
Obtain retrospective business and compliance sign-off within 2 business days of deployment.
Log the emergency change in the exception register regardless of outcome.
checklist.done: every emergency change has a ticket, retrospective sign-off within 2 business days, and an exception register entry.

checklist.step: Report configuration-accuracy metrics to the Product Oversight Committee
actions: Compile deployments completed, UAT defect rate, and any production mismatches for the period.
Present the metrics at the standing POC governance item.
Record any committee direction in the minutes.
checklist.done: configuration-accuracy metrics are presented at every POC sitting with directions recorded.

testing.step: Build the population of configuration deployments in the period
actions: Extract from the change management tool every deployed ticket implementing an approved product change in the period.
Reconcile the count to the release-gate log for the same period.
Resolve any difference before sampling.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to the release-gate log and signed complete.

testing.step: Match every deployment to a dated product owner sign-off
actions: Match each population row to its ticket's business sign-off date.
Confirm the sign-off pre-dates the deployment timestamp.
List unmatched or out-of-order rows as exceptions.
testing.done: every deployment is matched to a pre-dated sign-off or logged as an exception.

testing.step: Select and document the test sample
actions: Take 100% of deployments flagged as emergency/out-of-cycle changes.
Take a random sample of at least 20% of remaining deployments, minimum 15.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and covers all emergency changes.

testing.step: Re-perform the field-by-field comparison for sampled deployments
actions: Independently pull the deployed configuration and the approved source document for each sampled ticket.
Compare field by field without referencing the original comparison log.
Log any discrepancy as an exception, including discrepancies the original review missed.
testing.done: each sampled deployment has an independent comparison note with any discrepancy logged.

testing.step: Recompute a rating scenario for sampled rate/rule changes
actions: Select two rating scenarios per sampled rate change and independently calculate the expected premium from the approved rate exhibit.
Quote the same scenarios in the production rating engine and compare.
Log any variance beyond rounding tolerance as an exception.
testing.done: recomputed premiums match production output within tolerance for every sampled rate change, or are logged.

testing.step: Trace production effective dates against the approved go-live date
actions: For each sampled deployment, confirm the production effective date matches the approved go-live date and no earlier.
Check no in-force policy was re-rated or re-worded retroactively without a documented reason.
Log any early or retroactive application as an exception.
testing.done: no sampled deployment applied before its approved go-live date without a documented, approved reason.

testing.step: Check access control evidence for the sampled deployments
actions: Confirm the deployer identity on each sampled deployment log is on the authorised production-access list.
Confirm segregation between builder, peer reviewer and deployer where the procedure requires it.
Log any access-control gap as an exception.
testing.done: every sampled deployment shows an authorised deployer and required segregation, or a logged exception.

testing.step: Verify emergency changes received retrospective sign-off within the deadline
actions: Pull the retrospective sign-off date for every sampled emergency change.
Compare against the 2-business-day requirement from deployment.
Log any late or missing retrospective sign-off as an exception.
testing.done: every sampled emergency change has a retrospective sign-off within 2 business days or a logged exception.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with the ticket id, field affected and customer impact.
Assign root cause and owner, and set a remediation date.
For any wording/rate mismatch that reached customers, open a redress assessment.
Carry open exceptions into the next quarter's test as mandatory retest rows.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance threshold for wording/rate mismatch.
Write the conclusion with evidence references.
Have the independent QA reviewer, who built or reviewed none of the sampled tickets, sign the workpaper.
Report results to the Product Oversight Committee and file the workpaper.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion is filed and reported to the POC.

checklist.step: Log the inbound regulator query the day it is received
actions: Open a new correspondence record in the tracker the same business day the letter or FCA Connect message is received.
Enter the sender, reference number, subject matter, stated response deadline and the underlying filing or notification it relates to.
Scan and attach the original correspondence to the record.
Notify the Regulatory Counsel and the relevant business owner (Product, Distribution or Compliance) of the new query.
checklist.done: the correspondence record is created same-day with sender, deadline and the original document attached.

checklist.step: Compute the internal response deadline with buffer
actions: Read the stated deadline in the letter (typically 10-20 business days) and enter it on the record.
Back off an internal drafting deadline of at least 3 business days before the stated deadline for counsel review.
Load both dates into the correspondence tracker calendar with reminders.
Where the deadline is unreasonable given the query's scope, request an extension from the FCA case officer in writing and log the request.
checklist.done: the record shows both the stated and internal deadlines, loaded into the tracker with reminders.

checklist.step: Assign a response owner and gather the underlying facts
actions: Assign the query to the business owner best placed to answer (e.g. Insurance Product Manager for a product query, Distribution Specialist for a sales query).
Ask the owner to pull the underlying records: filing history, sales data, complaint files or system logs referenced by the query.
Set an internal check-in at the midpoint of the response window to confirm facts are on track.
checklist.done: a named owner has been assigned and the underlying facts are being assembled ahead of the midpoint check-in.

checklist.step: Draft the response addressing every question asked
actions: List every question or information request in the letter as its own numbered item.
Draft an answer to each numbered item, citing the underlying record or data source relied on.
Avoid answering questions not asked and avoid volunteering information outside the query's scope without a deliberate decision to do so.
Circulate the draft to the business owner for factual accuracy sign-off.
checklist.done: a draft response answers every numbered question with a cited source and has business factual sign-off.

checklist.step: Clear the draft through Regulatory Counsel and Head of Compliance
actions: Review the draft for accuracy, completeness and tone.
Confirm no admission or characterisation is made that has not been separately agreed with Head of Compliance.
Approve the draft for dispatch or return with named required changes.
Record the clearance date on the correspondence record.
checklist.done: General Counsel's dated clearance is recorded before dispatch.

checklist.step: Dispatch the response before the stated deadline
actions: Send the cleared response via the same channel the query arrived on (FCA Connect, portal upload, or letter) referencing the original case number.
Capture the send confirmation (portal receipt, delivery confirmation or postal tracking) and attach it to the correspondence record.
Update the record status to 'Responded' with the dispatch date and time.
Confirm the dispatch date is on or before the stated deadline; if not, proceed to the exception step.
checklist.done: the response is sent on or before the stated deadline with a captured send confirmation.

checklist.step: Where the deadline cannot be met, request an extension in writing before it lapses
actions: As soon as a missed deadline is foreseeable, write to the FCA case officer requesting a specific new date and stating the reason.
Copy Regulatory Counsel and Head of Compliance on the request.
Log the request and any granted extension on the correspondence record, updating the tracked deadline.
Never let the original deadline pass without either a response or a logged extension request.
checklist.done: any at-risk deadline has a written extension request logged before it lapses, with the outcome recorded.

checklist.step: Track any follow-up questions from the FCA as a linked thread
actions: Where the FCA responds with further questions, open a linked correspondence record referencing the original case number.
Apply the same deadline-computation and clearance steps to the follow-up.
Keep the full thread visible on the original record for continuity.
checklist.done: every follow-up is logged as a linked record with its own deadline and clearance trail.

checklist.step: Close the case only once the FCA confirms no further action or the matter concludes
actions: Wait for the FCA's closing communication (no further questions, case closed, or supervisory outcome).
Attach the closing communication to the correspondence record and set status to 'Closed'.
Where the FCA outcome requires a remediation action, open a linked action item with an owner and due date.
checklist.done: the record is closed only against a captured FCA closing communication, with any required remediation opened separately.

checklist.step: File the full correspondence trail in the compliance evidence repository
actions: Copy the inbound query, draft, clearance record, dispatched response and closing communication into the compliance evidence repository.
Apply the 6-year retention label from response date.
Confirm the entry is searchable by FCA case reference.
checklist.done: the full trail is filed, retention-labelled and searchable by case reference.

checklist.step: Review open correspondence weekly for at-risk deadlines
actions: Pull all open correspondence records weekly, sorted by days remaining to deadline.
Escalate anything inside the internal drafting deadline with no draft yet started.
Record the escalation outcome on the record.
checklist.done: at-risk correspondence is reviewed weekly with escalations recorded.

checklist.step: Brief senior management on material or thematic correspondence
actions: Identify correspondence that signals a thematic review, enforcement interest or cross-firm request.
Brief the Chief Compliance Officer and relevant Executive Committee member before the response is finalised.
Record the briefing date on the correspondence record.
checklist.done: material or thematic correspondence is briefed to senior management before response, with the date recorded.

checklist.step: Restrict who can communicate with the regulator on a case
actions: Name the single authorised point of contact for each correspondence case on the record.
Instruct business owners that all regulator contact routes through that named point of contact.
Log any unauthorised direct contact as an exception and brief the individual involved.
checklist.done: each case has a named single point of contact, with any breach logged and addressed.

checklist.step: Reconcile the correspondence tracker to the case management mailbox monthly
actions: Compare the correspondence tracker against the regulatory correspondence mailbox/portal inbox for the month.
Confirm every inbound item has a matching tracker record.
Log any untracked item as a control gap and open it retrospectively.
checklist.done: every mailbox/portal item for the month has a matching tracker record, with gaps opened retrospectively.

checklist.step: Report correspondence-handling metrics to the Compliance Committee quarterly
actions: Compile volume, on-time response rate and any extensions granted for the quarter.
Present to the Compliance Committee with commentary on any thematic pattern.
Record committee direction in the minutes.
checklist.done: correspondence metrics are reported to the Compliance Committee each quarter with directions recorded.

testing.step: Build the population of regulator correspondence closed in the period
actions: Extract every correspondence record with status 'Closed' or 'Responded' in the test period from the tracker.
Reconcile the extract to the regulatory correspondence mailbox/portal inbox for the same period.
Resolve any count difference before sampling.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to the mailbox/portal and signed complete.

testing.step: Compare every response dispatch date to its stated deadline
actions: For each population row, compare the dispatch date to the stated deadline (or any logged, granted extension).
List every row where dispatch is later than the applicable deadline as an automatic exception.
testing.done: every population row is checked against its deadline, with lates listed as exceptions.

testing.step: Select and document the test sample
actions: Take 100% of correspondence flagged thematic, enforcement-related, or briefed to senior management.
Take a random sample of 25% of the remainder, minimum 10 items.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and covers all thematic/enforcement items.

testing.step: Re-read the response against every question the FCA actually asked
actions: For each sampled item, list the questions from the original letter independently.
Check the dispatched response answers every one, with no question skipped or answered incompletely.
Log any gap as an exception.
testing.done: every sampled response is checked question-by-question with gaps logged.

testing.step: Confirm counsel clearance pre-dates dispatch for the sample
actions: Pull the General Counsel clearance date and the dispatch date for each sampled item.
Confirm clearance pre-dates dispatch.
Log any response dispatched without a pre-dated clearance as an exception.
testing.done: every sampled dispatch has pre-dated clearance evidence, or is logged as an exception.

testing.step: Verify the single-point-of-contact control on the sample
actions: Check the named point of contact recorded on each sampled case.
Confirm no other individual's correspondence with the FCA appears in the case file.
Log any unauthorised contact found as an exception.
testing.done: every sampled case shows a single authorised point of contact, or a logged exception.

testing.step: Trace extension requests to a granted outcome for the sample
actions: For sampled items with a logged extension request, confirm the FCA's written grant and the revised deadline used.
Confirm dispatch respected the revised deadline, not the original.
Log any extension used without a written grant as an exception.
testing.done: every sampled extension is backed by a written grant and a respected revised deadline.

testing.step: Confirm evidence completeness in the compliance evidence repository
actions: For each sampled item, confirm the inbound query, draft, clearance and dispatched response are all present in the repository.
Confirm the retention label is applied and the entry is searchable by case reference.
Log any missing artifact as an exception.
testing.done: every sampled item's full evidence set is present, labelled and searchable, or logged as an exception.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with the case reference and what was missed.
Assign root cause and owner, and set a remediation date.
For missed deadlines, assess whether a proactive notification to the FCA is required and route to General Counsel.
Carry open exceptions into the next quarter's test as mandatory retest rows.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the on-time response rate and compare to the zero-tolerance threshold for missed deadlines.
Write the conclusion referencing the evidence reviewed.
Have the independent reviewer, who drafted none of the sampled responses, sign the workpaper.
Report results to the Compliance Committee and file the workpaper in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion is filed and reported to the Compliance Committee.

checklist.step: Capture every approval artifact into the archive at the point of approval
actions: On POC sign-off, copy the pack, minutes and conditions log into the document management repository under the product folder.
On configuration deployment, copy the build ticket, comparison log and UAT report into the same folder.
On closure of any regulator correspondence, copy the full thread into the same folder.
Confirm every capture completes within 5 business days of the triggering event.
checklist.done: every triggering event has its artifact captured in the product folder within 5 business days.

checklist.step: Index each record with the standard metadata fields
actions: Tag each record with product name, product version, approval type, approval date and retention start date.
Confirm the record is searchable by each of those fields in the repository search index.
Reject and return for re-indexing any record filed without the full metadata set.
checklist.done: every record carries the full metadata set and is confirmed searchable on each field.

checklist.step: Version-control the filed product document set
actions: Maintain a single master folder per product with a sub-version for every approved wording, rate exhibit or rule set.
Mark exactly one version per product line as 'current' at any time; supersede prior versions rather than deleting them.
Cross-reference each version to its approval date and the policies issued under it.
checklist.done: each product's master folder shows a clear version history with exactly one current version marked.

checklist.step: Apply the correct retention period and legal-hold flag
actions: Apply the 6-year-from-withdrawal retention label to every captured record.
Check the legal hold register for any open litigation or FCA investigation touching the product; apply a hold flag that suspends the retention clock where one exists.
Review the legal hold register monthly for holds that can now be released.
checklist.done: every record carries a retention label, and any applicable legal hold is flagged and reviewed monthly.

checklist.step: Control disposal so nothing is destroyed before its retention period ends
actions: Run the repository's disposal-due report monthly, listing records whose retention period has lapsed.
Check each listed record for an active legal hold before scheduling disposal.
Route the disposal list to the Head of Compliance for sign-off before any record is destroyed.
Log the disposal sign-off and execution date.
checklist.done: no record is disposed of without a monthly disposal-due check, hold check, and Head of Compliance sign-off.

checklist.step: Reconcile the archive against the release-gate and configuration logs monthly
actions: Pull the month's closed release-gate records and configuration tickets.
Match each to an archive entry with the full artifact set.
Log any release-gate or ticket with no matching archive entry as a control gap and remediate within the month.
checklist.done: every closed release-gate record and ticket has a matching archive entry, with gaps remediated in-month.

checklist.step: Test retrievability with a blind pull quarterly
actions: Select a product at random without advance notice to the archive team.
Time how long it takes to produce the full approval and version history from the repository.
Log the pull time against the 5-business-day regulator-response target and flag any product that would miss it.
checklist.done: a blind retrieval drill is run quarterly with the pull time logged against the 5-day target.

checklist.step: Restrict write and delete access to the archive
actions: Review the access list for the document management repository's product-approval area quarterly.
Confirm only Records Manager and named delegates hold write/delete permission; all others are read-only.
Remove or flag any access held outside that population.
checklist.done: write/delete access is limited to the authorised population, confirmed quarterly.

checklist.step: Reconstruct any record found missing during reconciliation or testing
actions: Identify the original source system or owner for the missing artifact.
Request a reissued or reconstructed copy and note it as a reconstruction in the metadata.
Have Compliance Analyst sign off the reconstruction as complete.
checklist.done: every identified gap is reconstructed, flagged as such, and signed off by Compliance Analyst.

checklist.step: Respond to an FCA record request within the committed window
actions: On receipt of a request, pull the full approval and version history for the named product from the repository.
Package the extract with an index sheet and route to Head of Compliance for clearance.
Dispatch within 5 business days and log the dispatch date on the request record.
checklist.done: the requested record set is cleared and dispatched within 5 business days, logged on the request record.

checklist.step: Maintain a records-management training programme for the archive team
actions: Deliver indexing and retention-rule training to every team member handling approval records at onboarding and annually.
Test understanding with a short scenario quiz.
Log completion in the training system.
checklist.done: every archive team member has current, logged training on indexing and retention rules.

checklist.step: Report archive completeness and retrieval performance to Compliance Committee
actions: Compile completeness rate, disposal actions and blind-drill retrieval times for the quarter.
Present to the Compliance Committee.
Record any committee direction in the minutes.
checklist.done: archive performance is reported to the Compliance Committee each quarter with directions recorded.

checklist.step: Migrate legacy paper or superseded-system records into the current repository
actions: Identify any product approval record still held only in a superseded system or physical file.
Scan or export it into the current document management repository with full metadata.
Retire the legacy holding once migration is confirmed complete.
checklist.done: no in-scope record remains solely in a superseded or physical-only location.

checklist.step: Audit trail every access and edit to a filed approval record
actions: Confirm the repository logs every view, edit and export of an approval record with user id and timestamp.
Review the audit log monthly for edits to records outside a reconstruction workflow.
Escalate any unexplained edit to Records Manager and Head of Compliance.
checklist.done: the repository's audit log is reviewed monthly with any unexplained edit escalated.

checklist.step: Confirm business continuity coverage for the archive system
actions: Confirm the document management repository is included in the annual business continuity/disaster recovery test.
Verify records can be restored from backup within the recovery time objective.
Log the test result and any remediation needed.
checklist.done: the archive is confirmed in-scope for BC/DR testing with a logged, current test result.

testing.step: Build the population of approval events in the period
actions: Extract every POC sign-off, configuration deployment and closed regulator correspondence from the period.
Reconcile the count to the release-gate log and correspondence tracker for the same period.
Resolve any count difference before sampling.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to source logs and signed complete.

testing.step: Match every event to a complete archive entry
actions: Match each population row to its archive folder entry.
Confirm the full artifact set (pack, correspondence, or config evidence as applicable) is present.
List any missing or incomplete entry as an exception.
testing.done: every event is matched to a complete archive entry or logged as an exception.

testing.step: Select and document the test sample
actions: Take 100% of products currently under legal hold.
Take a random sample of 25% of the remainder, minimum 15 records.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and covers all legal-hold products.

testing.step: Verify metadata completeness on the sample
actions: Check each sampled record carries product name, version, approval type, approval date and retention start date.
Confirm the record is retrievable by search on each field.
Log any missing metadata field as an exception.
testing.done: every sampled record has complete, searchable metadata or a logged exception.

testing.step: Run a timed blind retrieval on sampled products
actions: Request the full approval and version history for 5 sampled products without advance notice to the archive team.
Time the retrieval against the 5-business-day regulator-response target.
Log any retrieval that would miss the target as an exception.
testing.done: a timed blind retrieval is completed for 5 sampled products with results logged.

testing.step: Confirm no disposal occurred before retention or hold clearance on the sample
actions: Check the disposal log for any sampled product with a retention date not yet lapsed or an active legal hold.
Confirm none were disposed of.
Log any premature disposal as a reportable exception.
testing.done: no sampled product shows premature disposal, or the breach is logged and escalated.

testing.step: Test access-control evidence on the archive
actions: Pull the current write/delete access list for the product-approval archive area.
Confirm it matches the authorised population from the quarterly review.
Log any unauthorised access as an exception.
testing.done: the archive access list matches the authorised population, or gaps are logged.

testing.step: Check version-control integrity on the sample
actions: For each sampled product, confirm exactly one version is marked 'current' and prior versions are superseded, not deleted.
Cross-check the current version against the most recent configuration deployment record.
Log any mismatch as an exception.
testing.done: every sampled product shows correct version control matching the latest deployment, or a logged exception.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with the product name and record missing/affected.
Assign root cause and owner, and set a remediation date.
For any premature disposal, escalate to General Counsel for a litigation-risk assessment.
Carry open exceptions into the next quarter's test as mandatory retest rows.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the completeness rate against the zero-tolerance threshold for missing core records.
Write the conclusion referencing the evidence reviewed.
Have the independent Internal Auditor, outside the Records team, sign the workpaper.
Report results to the Compliance Committee and file the workpaper in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion is filed and reported to the Compliance Committee.

checklist.step: Screen every party at quote and pre-bind
actions: Confirm the Underwriting Platform's bind workflow calls the sanctions screening system automatically for every named insured, joint policyholder and named beneficiary before the bind button is enabled.
In the screening system, review the fuzzy-match algorithm's match threshold setting quarterly against the vendor's recommended calibration.
Confirm the bind workflow blocks completion until the screening system returns a 'clear' or a disposed hit.
Log the screening system's transaction id against the policy number in the underwriting file.
checklist.done: every bind is technically blocked pending a clear or disposed screening result, logged against the policy number.

checklist.step: Triage every screening hit within one business day
actions: Open each hit in the screening system's case queue and compare name, date of birth, nationality and address against the Consolidated List entry.
Classify as true match, false positive, or requiring further information, using the documented matching criteria.
For a suspected true match, immediately place the transaction on hold and escalate to the Financial Crime AML Officer.
Record the disposition, reasoning and reviewer identity in the case queue before closing the hit.
checklist.done: every hit is triaged within 1 business day with a documented disposition and, for true matches, an immediate hold.

checklist.step: Freeze assets and funds on a confirmed match
actions: On confirmation of a true match, instruct the Billing Operations Manager to freeze any premium refund, cash value or claims payment associated with the party.
Record the freeze instruction, amount and account/policy reference in the sanctions case file.
Ensure no further transaction (renewal, endorsement, payment) processes on the frozen policy without OFSI licence.
checklist.done: every confirmed match has a documented, executed freeze with no further transaction processed unlicensed.

checklist.step: Report the confirmed match to OFSI without delay
actions: Complete the OFSI reporting form via the OFSI online reporting service with designated person details, nature of funds/assets frozen, and the freeze date.
Submit the report the same or next business day after confirmation — 'without delay' under the Sanctions and Anti-Money Laundering Act 2018.
Retain the OFSI submission receipt and any reference number in the sanctions case file.
Diarise any OFSI follow-up request and respond within the timeframe OFSI sets.
checklist.done: the OFSI report is submitted without delay with a retained submission receipt.

checklist.step: Rescreen the entire in-force book on every Consolidated List update
actions: Confirm the screening system's automated Consolidated List feed updates within 1 business day of an OFSI publication.
Trigger a full in-force book batch rescreen against the updated list.
Route any new hit generated by the update through the same triage process as a fresh hit.
Log the rescreen run date, list version and hit count.
checklist.done: a full-book rescreen runs against every list update within 1 business day, with hits triaged and the run logged.

checklist.step: Screen beneficiary and payee changes at the point of change
actions: When a beneficiary or payee is added or changed on a policy, trigger a screening system check for the new party before the change is saved.
Block saving the change until the screening result returns clear or is disposed.
Log the screening transaction id against the change record.
checklist.done: no beneficiary/payee change saves without a completed screening check logged against it.

checklist.step: Screen claims payees before claim payment release
actions: Before releasing any claims payment, confirm the payee has a clear or disposed screening result dated within the payment authorisation window.
Where the payee is new to the claim (e.g. a repairer, medical provider or third-party beneficiary), screen them before payment.
Block payment release in the Claims Platform until screening is confirmed clear.
Log the screening reference against the payment record.
checklist.done: every claims payment is blocked until the payee's screening result is confirmed clear, logged against the payment.

checklist.step: Maintain and calibrate the fuzzy-match screening rules
actions: Review false-positive and false-negative rates from the case queue monthly.
Propose threshold or transliteration-rule adjustments to the Financial Crime AML Officer where the rate drifts outside tolerance.
Document any approved rule change with the before/after setting and effective date.
checklist.done: matching rule performance is reviewed monthly with any change documented and approved.

checklist.step: Escalate any attempt to circumvent screening
actions: Where a bind, change or payment is found processed without a screening record, immediately notify the Financial Crime AML Officer.
Retroactively screen the party the same day and place the policy on hold pending result.
Log the bypass as an exception with the system or process gap identified.
checklist.done: every discovered bypass is retroactively screened same-day and logged as an exception with the gap identified.

checklist.step: Reconcile screening logs to the bind/renewal/payment population monthly
actions: Extract all binds, renewals, beneficiary changes and claims payments for the month from source systems.
Match each to a screening system transaction log entry.
Log any unmatched transaction as a control gap for immediate investigation.
checklist.done: every in-scope transaction for the month is matched to a screening log entry, with gaps investigated immediately.

checklist.step: Maintain the sanctions case file for regulator inspection
actions: File every hit disposition, freeze instruction and OFSI report in the compliance evidence repository under the party name.
Apply the 5-year-from-relationship-end retention label.
Confirm the file is retrievable by party name and OFSI reference.
checklist.done: sanctions case files are filed, retention-labelled and retrievable by party name and OFSI reference.

checklist.step: Train underwriting, claims and policy admin staff on sanctions red flags
actions: Deliver sanctions awareness training covering red flags and the mandatory hold procedure at onboarding and annually.
Test understanding with a scenario-based assessment.
Log completion in the learning management system.
checklist.done: underwriting, claims and policy admin staff hold current, logged sanctions training.

checklist.step: Review the sanctions programme's effectiveness with senior management
actions: Compile hit volume, true-match count, freeze actions and OFSI reports for the quarter.
Present to the Risk Committee alongside any thematic finding.
Record committee direction in the minutes.
checklist.done: sanctions programme effectiveness is reported to the Risk Committee each quarter with directions recorded.

checklist.step: Test business continuity of the screening system
actions: Confirm the sanctions screening system is in-scope for the annual BC/DR test.
Verify a manual screening fallback procedure exists for a system outage, using the OFSI website search as the documented manual method.
Log the test result and any remediation needed.
checklist.done: the screening system is BC/DR tested with a documented manual fallback procedure.

checklist.step: Audit third-party screening vendor performance annually
actions: Review the screening vendor's list-update SLA performance and false-positive rate reporting for the year.
Confirm the vendor's own sanctions and financial crime controls via their SOC report or equivalent attestation.
Report findings to the Financial Crime AML Officer.
checklist.done: the screening vendor's annual performance and control attestation are reviewed and reported.

testing.step: Build the population of in-scope transactions in the period
actions: Extract every new business bind, renewal, beneficiary change and claims payment from the period across policy admin and claims systems.
Reconcile the extract to the screening system's transaction log count for the same period.
Resolve any count difference before sampling.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to the screening log and signed complete.

testing.step: Match every transaction to a completed screening result
actions: Match each population row to a screening transaction id with a clear or disposed result.
Confirm the screening date pre-dates or coincides with the transaction date.
List unmatched or out-of-order rows as automatic exceptions.
testing.done: every transaction is matched to a pre-dated screening result or logged as an exception.

testing.step: Select and document the test sample
actions: Take 100% of transactions that generated a screening hit.
Take a random sample of 10% of the remaining clear population, minimum 25 transactions.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and covers all hit-generating transactions.

testing.step: Re-perform the hit disposition for sampled hits
actions: Independently review each sampled hit's name, DOB, nationality and address against the Consolidated List entry as it stood on the disposition date.
Reach an independent match/no-match conclusion without viewing the original disposition first.
Compare to the recorded disposition; log any disagreement as an exception.
testing.done: each sampled hit has an independent re-performance note with disagreements logged.

testing.step: Trace confirmed matches to a freeze instruction and OFSI report
actions: For every sampled true match, confirm a freeze instruction was executed and an OFSI report was submitted.
Compare the confirmation date to the report submission date; flag anything not submitted the same or next business day.
Treat a missing or late OFSI report as a reportable breach, not a documentation exception.
testing.done: every sampled true match traces to an executed freeze and a same/next-business-day OFSI report, or is escalated.

testing.step: Verify the full-book rescreen ran on every list update in the period
actions: Pull the OFSI Consolidated List publication dates for the period.
Match each to a logged full-book rescreen run within 1 business day.
Log any missed or late rescreen as an exception.
testing.done: every list update in the period has a matched, timely rescreen run, or a logged exception.

testing.step: Check claims payment holds on the sample
actions: For sampled claims payments, confirm the payment release date is on or after the payee's screening clear date.
Check no payment released before screening completed.
Log any early release as an exception.
testing.done: no sampled claims payment released before payee screening completed, or the breach is logged.

testing.step: Test the manual fallback procedure was available during any outage
actions: Check the screening system's uptime log for any outage in the period.
For any outage, confirm the manual OFSI-website fallback procedure was invoked and documented.
Log any transaction processed during an outage without the fallback as an exception.
testing.done: any outage period shows the fallback procedure invoked, or affected transactions are logged as exceptions.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with the transaction id and what was missed.
Assign root cause and owner, and set a remediation date.
For any unscreened bound policy or unfrozen match, open an immediate remediation with the Chief Risk Officer.
Carry open exceptions into the next quarter's test as mandatory retest rows.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance threshold for unscreened bound transactions.
Write the conclusion referencing the evidence reviewed.
Have the independent Financial Crime Investigator, who disposed of none of the sampled hits, sign the workpaper.
Report results to the Risk Committee and file the workpaper in the evidence repository.

checklist.step: Confirm the MLRO appointment is current and properly authorised

Confirm the appointment is at a sufficiently senior level with direct Board or Risk Committee access.
Where the MLRO role is vacant or the incumbent is on extended leave, appoint a deputy MLRO within 5 business days and record the interim arrangement.
File the current appointment letter in the compliance evidence repository.
checklist.done: a current, Board-confirmed MLRO appointment is on file, with any vacancy covered by a deputy within 5 business days.

checklist.step: Refresh the firm-wide money laundering and terrorist financing risk assessment
actions: Update the risk assessment covering customer, product, channel, and geographic risk factors relevant to the in-scope life/investment products.
Incorporate the latest National Risk Assessment and FCA sector findings.
Score each risk factor and set the resulting overall firm risk rating.
Circulate the draft to Chief Risk Officer for review.
checklist.done: an updated risk assessment with a current firm risk rating is drafted and routed for review.

checklist.step: Update the AML policy and CDD/EDD standards to reflect the risk assessment
actions: Revise the AML policy's customer due diligence and enhanced due diligence sections to match the current risk assessment's findings.
Set out the PEP identification and EDD trigger criteria explicitly, including beneficial-ownership verification steps.
Version the policy document and log the change summary against the prior version.
Route the revised policy for legal and Compliance review.
checklist.done: the AML policy is revised, versioned, and matches the current risk assessment's risk factors.

checklist.step: Obtain Board or Risk Committee approval of the policy and risk assessment
actions: Submit the policy and risk assessment to the Board or delegated Risk Committee at least 10 business days ahead of the sitting.
Present the key changes and the resulting firm risk rating.
Record the approval date and any conditions in the Board minutes.
File the approved documents and minutes in the compliance evidence repository.
checklist.done: a dated Board/Risk Committee approval is recorded and the approved documents are filed.

checklist.step: Cascade the updated policy and standards to affected teams
actions: Publish the approved policy to the underwriting, claims, policy admin and distribution teams via the intranet/policy library.
Brief the relevant Heads of Department on any material change to CDD/EDD triggers.
Confirm acknowledgement of receipt from each department head.
checklist.done: the updated policy is published and acknowledged by every affected department head.

checklist.step: Confirm the AML case management platform reflects the current risk rating and triggers
actions: In the AML platform's rule configuration, update customer risk scoring weights to match the approved risk assessment.
Confirm EDD workflow triggers fire correctly for the PEP and high-risk criteria set out in the policy.
Test the updated rules against a sample of known high-risk and low-risk profiles before go-live.
Record the configuration change and test results.
checklist.done: the AML platform's rules match the approved policy and are tested before go-live.

checklist.step: Review MLRO independence and resourcing annually
actions: Confirm the MLRO's reporting line does not create a conflict with commercial or sales targets.
Assess whether the AML team's headcount and tooling are adequate against the current transaction and case volumes.
Document any resourcing gap and the remediation plan.
checklist.done: MLRO independence and resourcing are documented as adequate, or a remediation plan is recorded.

checklist.step: Maintain the MLRO's suspicious activity oversight log
actions: Maintain a running log of internal suspicion reports received and considered, separate from the SAR filing record.
Record the MLRO's disposition and reasoning for every internal report, including 'no SAR required' decisions.
Review the log's completeness monthly.
checklist.done: a complete, monthly-reviewed internal suspicion oversight log is maintained by the MLRO.

checklist.step: Report AML programme status to the Board at least annually
actions: Prepare the MLRO annual report covering risk assessment changes, SAR volumes, training completion, and any regulatory findings.
Present the report to the Board or Risk Committee.
Record the Board's response and any directed actions in the minutes.
checklist.done: an MLRO annual report is presented to the Board with directed actions recorded.

checklist.step: Track policy review due dates and escalate any at risk of lapsing
actions: Maintain the governance calendar entry for the AML policy's annual review date.
Escalate to the Financial Crime AML Officer at T-60 and T-30 days if the review has not started.
Escalate to Chief Risk Officer if the review date is at risk of lapsing with no Board sitting scheduled.
checklist.done: the review date is tracked with escalations at T-60/T-30 and to Chief Risk Officer if at risk.

checklist.step: Record any interim policy amendment outside the annual cycle

Log the interim amendment against the policy version history with the triggering regulatory change cited.
Confirm the next annual review still occurs on schedule regardless of the interim amendment.
checklist.done: interim amendments are approved, version-logged, and do not displace the scheduled annual review.

checklist.step: Coordinate the AML programme with the wider Financial Crime function

Confirm cross-referral processes exist between AML, sanctions and fraud case queues.
Document the coordination meeting outcomes.
checklist.done: quarterly cross-function coordination is documented with confirmed cross-referral processes.

checklist.step: File the approved programme documents in the compliance evidence repository

Apply the 5-year-from-supersession retention label.
Confirm the entry is searchable by document type and approval date.
checklist.done: the programme documents are filed, retention-labelled and searchable.

checklist.step: Benchmark the programme against FCA thematic findings
actions: Review any published FCA thematic review or Dear CEO letter relevant to life/investment AML controls.
Assess the firm's programme against the findings and document any gap.
Route identified gaps into the policy update cycle.
checklist.done: the programme is benchmarked against current FCA thematic findings with gaps routed for remediation.

checklist.step: Confirm Board-level AML competency and challenge
actions: Confirm at least one Board member or Risk Committee member has documented financial-crime competency or receives targeted briefing ahead of AML approvals.
Log attendance and questions raised at the AML approval sitting in the minutes.
Flag to the Chair any sitting where the AML item received no substantive challenge.
checklist.done: Board-level AML competency and challenge is documented for every approval sitting.

testing.step: Confirm the current AML policy and risk assessment are within their review cycle
actions: Pull the current policy version and its Board approval date.
Confirm the approval date is within the last 12 months (or an approved interim amendment is on file).
Log an expired review as an automatic exception.
testing.done: the current policy is confirmed within its 12-month cycle, or the lapse is logged.

testing.step: Confirm continuous MLRO coverage across the period
actions: Pull the MLRO/deputy appointment history for the test period from Board minutes and HR records.
Confirm no gap in coverage exceeded 5 business days.
Log any uncovered gap as an exception.
testing.done: continuous MLRO coverage is confirmed for the period, or gaps are logged.

testing.step: Select and document the test sample for CDD/EDD case review
actions: Take 100% of cases flagged EDD/PEP in the AML platform during the period.
Take a random sample of 10% of standard CDD cases, minimum 20.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and covers all EDD/PEP cases.

testing.step: Re-perform the CDD/EDD assessment for sampled cases
actions: Independently pull identification, verification and beneficial-ownership evidence for each sampled case.
Reach an independent CDD/EDD-adequacy conclusion against the current policy standard.
Log any disagreement with the original assessment as an exception.
testing.done: each sampled case has an independent re-performance note with disagreements logged.

testing.step: Verify AML platform rule configuration matches the approved policy
actions: Pull the platform's current risk-scoring weights and EDD trigger configuration.
Compare against the approved policy's stated criteria.
Log any mismatch as an exception.
testing.done: platform configuration matches the approved policy, or the mismatch is logged.

testing.step: Test the MLRO's independence and internal reporting line
actions: Review the MLRO's reporting line and remuneration structure for commercial conflicts.
Interview the MLRO on access to the Board/Risk Committee.
Log any independence concern as a finding for Risk Committee attention.
testing.done: MLRO independence is assessed with any concern logged for Risk Committee attention.

testing.step: Check the internal suspicion oversight log for completeness
actions: Sample 10 internal suspicion reports from the log.
Confirm each has a documented MLRO disposition and reasoning.
Log any report with no recorded disposition as an exception.
testing.done: sampled internal reports show complete, reasoned MLRO dispositions, or gaps are logged.

testing.step: Confirm training completion evidence for the AML team
actions: Pull training completion records for the AML/Financial Crime team for the current cycle.
Confirm 100% completion against the required annual training.
Log any incomplete record as an exception.
testing.done: AML team training completion is confirmed at 100%, or gaps are logged.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with the case id or governance item affected.
Assign root cause and owner, and set a remediation date.
For any MLRO coverage gap, confirm Board notification occurred.
Carry open exceptions into the next annual test as mandatory retest rows.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Assess overall programme adequacy against the zero-tolerance thresholds for review-cycle lapse and MLRO coverage gaps.
Write the conclusion referencing the evidence reviewed.
Have the independent Internal Auditor, outside the AML function, sign the workpaper.
Report results to the Board and file the workpaper in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion is filed and reported to the Board.
