checklist.step: Capture the internal suspicion report at first identification
actions: Open an internal report case in the AML platform the moment a staff member, underwriter or claims handler flags a suspicion.
Record the reporting individual, the transaction/policy details, and the specific facts giving rise to suspicion.
Restrict case access to the AML team only, applying the platform's tipping-off access control.
Timestamp the case creation for the 24-hour disposition clock.
checklist.done: an access-restricted internal report case is created with full facts and a timestamp, same-day as identification.

checklist.step: Have the MLRO consider the report against the suspicion threshold
actions: Review the reported facts, any linked transaction history and prior screening/case data for the party.
Apply the 'reasonable grounds to suspect' threshold from the AML policy and reach a documented conclusion.
Where grounds exist, move immediately to the SAR drafting step; where they do not, record the reasoning for 'no SAR required'.
Complete this consideration within 5 business days of the report being opened.
checklist.done: the MLRO's documented consideration and conclusion is recorded within 5 business days of report opening.

checklist.step: Draft and submit the SAR via the NCA's SAR Online portal
actions: Log in to the NCA SAR Online portal and complete the SAR form with subject details, the suspicious activity description, and the relevant offence.
Where a prohibited act (e.g. paying a surrender value or claim) is pending, mark the SAR as requesting a Defence Against Money Laundering (DAML) and state the act and its timing.
Submit the SAR promptly following the MLRO's conclusion and capture the SAR Online reference number.
File the submission confirmation in the case.
checklist.done: the SAR is submitted via SAR Online with a captured reference number, DAML requested where a prohibited act is pending.

checklist.step: Hold any prohibited act until the DAML notice period expires or consent is given
actions: Instruct the relevant operational team (Claims, Policy Admin) to place the transaction on hold pending the DAML outcome.
Track the statutory notice period (7 working days) and the further moratorium period (31 days) if the NCA refuses consent.
Release the hold only on the earlier of explicit consent, the notice period expiring with no refusal, or the moratorium period expiring.
Record the hold start, DAML outcome and release date in the case.
checklist.done: the prohibited act is held until the DAML notice/moratorium period is correctly resolved, with dates recorded.

checklist.step: Apply tipping-off controls throughout the process
actions: Confirm no communication to the customer, broker or non-AML staff discloses that a SAR has been made or is contemplated (POCA s.333A).
Brief any operational team placing a hold using neutral wording (e.g. 'under review') that does not reveal the SAR.
Restrict the case file to the AML team and named legal advisers only.
Log any suspected tipping-off incident immediately to General Counsel.
checklist.done: no disclosure of the SAR reaches the customer or unauthorised staff, confirmed by the access log and briefing wording used.

checklist.step: Cross-reference the SAR to any linked sanctions or fraud case
actions: Check the sanctions screening system and the SIU fraud case queue for any existing case on the same party.
Link the cases where they exist and share relevant facts between teams under the appropriate information-sharing gateway.
Record the cross-reference in the AML case.
checklist.done: linked sanctions or fraud cases are identified and cross-referenced with shared facts recorded.

checklist.step: Respond to any NCA follow-up request on the SAR
actions: Monitor the SAR Online portal and the case mailbox for any NCA request for further information.
Gather the requested detail from operational systems and respond within the timeframe the NCA sets.
Log the request and response on the case.
checklist.done: every NCA follow-up is logged with a response within the NCA's set timeframe.

checklist.step: Maintain the SAR submission log separate from case narrative detail
actions: Record each SAR's reference number, submission date, DAML status and outcome on a controlled submission log.
Restrict the log's narrative-detail columns to authorised viewers only.
Reconcile the log to SAR Online's submission history monthly.
checklist.done: the submission log is maintained, access-restricted, and reconciled to SAR Online monthly.

checklist.step: Escalate any internal report left undecided past the target window
actions: Review the AML platform's open-case queue daily for reports approaching the 5-business-day disposition target.
Escalate any case at risk to a deputy MLRO for same-day decision.
Log the escalation and resulting decision.
checklist.done: no internal report exceeds the disposition target without a logged escalation and decision.

checklist.step: Notify affected operational teams once a hold can be released
actions: On DAML resolution, instruct the operational team in writing that the hold is released and the transaction may proceed.
Confirm the operational system reflects the release before any payment or change is processed.
Log the release instruction and confirmation.
checklist.done: operational holds are released only on a logged, written MLRO instruction, confirmed in the system.

checklist.step: File the complete SAR case in the restricted compliance evidence repository
actions: Copy the internal report, MLRO consideration notes, SAR submission confirmation and any DAML correspondence into a tipping-off-restricted repository area.
Apply the 5-year retention label from submission date.
Confirm only named AML and legal personnel have read access.
checklist.done: the SAR case is filed in a restricted area, retention-labelled, with access limited to named AML and legal staff.

checklist.step: Report SAR volumes and outcomes to the Board without disclosing subject identities inappropriately
actions: Compile aggregate SAR volume, DAML requests and outcomes for the reporting period.
Present the aggregate report to the Board or Risk Committee, withholding subject-identifying detail from wider circulation.
Record the Board's response in the minutes.
checklist.done: aggregate SAR reporting reaches the Board each period without inappropriate subject disclosure.

checklist.step: Train staff on internal reporting obligations and tipping-off risk
actions: Deliver training on how and when to raise an internal suspicion report and the tipping-off offence under POCA s.333A.
Test understanding with scenario-based questions on customer conversations during a hold.
Log completion in the learning management system.
checklist.done: staff hold current, logged training on internal reporting and tipping-off risk.

checklist.step: Review 'no SAR required' decisions for pattern risk
actions: Periodically review the aggregate of 'no SAR required' MLRO decisions for concentration by product, region or distribution channel.
Assess whether a pattern suggests the suspicion threshold or reporting culture needs review.
Document the assessment and any resulting action.
checklist.done: a periodic pattern review of 'no SAR' decisions is documented with any resulting action.

checklist.step: Confirm segregation between the SAR decision-maker and the underlying transaction
actions: Confirm the MLRO or deputy considering a SAR has no direct commercial relationship with the transaction or customer.
Where a conflict exists, confirm an alternate deputy made the decision.
Log the segregation check outcome.
checklist.done: segregation between decision-maker and transaction is confirmed, with conflicts routed to an alternate deputy.

testing.step: Build the population of internal reports and SARs in the period
actions: Extract every internal suspicion report case opened in the AML platform during the period.
Reconcile the count against the SAR submission log for the same period.
Resolve any count difference before sampling.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to the submission log and signed complete.

testing.step: Check MLRO disposition timeliness for every report
actions: Compare each report's opening timestamp to its MLRO disposition date.
Flag any report exceeding the 5-business-day target with no logged escalation as an automatic exception.
testing.done: every report's disposition timeliness is checked, with unlogged delays flagged as exceptions.

testing.step: Select and document the test sample
actions: Take 100% of reports resulting in a DAML request.
Take a random sample of 30% of remaining reports, minimum 15.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and covers all DAML requests.

testing.step: Re-perform the suspicion-threshold assessment for sampled reports
actions: Independently review the facts of each sampled report against the 'reasonable grounds to suspect' threshold.
Reach an independent SAR/no-SAR conclusion without viewing the original MLRO decision first.
Log any disagreement with the recorded decision as an exception.
testing.done: each sampled report has an independent re-performance note with disagreements logged.

testing.step: Trace sampled SARs to their SAR Online submission
actions: For each sampled SAR, confirm the captured SAR Online reference number and submission date against the case file.
Confirm submission occurred promptly following the MLRO's conclusion.
Log any unexplained delay as an exception.
testing.done: every sampled SAR traces to a confirmed, prompt SAR Online submission or a logged exception.

testing.step: Verify no prohibited act proceeded without a resolved DAML
actions: For each sampled DAML case, confirm the operational hold start and release dates against the notice/moratorium period rules.
Confirm the prohibited act (payment, surrender) did not proceed before the period correctly resolved.
Treat any early release as a reportable breach, not a documentation exception.
testing.done: no sampled DAML case shows a prohibited act proceeding early, or the breach is escalated.

testing.step: Test tipping-off controls on the sample
actions: Review customer and broker correspondence linked to sampled hold periods for any disclosure of the SAR.
Confirm case access logs show only authorised AML/legal personnel viewed the case.
Log any suspected tipping-off incident as a reportable exception.
testing.done: no sampled case shows a tipping-off disclosure or unauthorised access, or the breach is escalated.

testing.step: Check aggregate Board reporting matches the underlying SAR log
actions: Compare the aggregate SAR volume reported to the Board for the period against the submission log total.
Confirm no material discrepancy exists.
Log any discrepancy as an exception.
testing.done: Board-reported SAR volumes match the submission log, or discrepancies are logged.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with the case reference and what was missed.
Assign root cause and owner, and set a remediation date.
For any early prohibited-act release or tipping-off incident, open an immediate escalation to General Counsel and consider self-report to the NCA/FCA.
Carry open exceptions into the next quarter's test as mandatory retest rows.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance threshold for early prohibited-act releases.
Write the conclusion referencing the evidence reviewed, without disclosing subject identities in the wider report.
Have the independent Internal Auditor, outside MLRO decision-making, sign the workpaper.
Report aggregate results to the Board and file the workpaper in the restricted evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion is filed and aggregate results are reported to the Board.

Version the curriculum and log the change summary against the prior version.

checklist.step: Build and publish the course in the learning management system

Publish the course and confirm it renders correctly on desktop and mobile.
Tag the course with the applicable audience groups (underwriting, claims, distribution, all-staff).
checklist.done: the course is published in Cornerstone LMS with a scored assessment and correct audience tagging.

checklist.step: Assign the course to every in-scope employee

checklist.done: the course is assigned to the full filtered roster, with new joiners auto-assigned on a 30-day clock.

checklist.step: Distribute training and attestation requirements to producers

Notify all active producers selling covered products of the annual requirement and the due date.
Track completion and attestation submission per producer in the portal.
Flag producers with no prior AML training on file for immediate assignment.
checklist.done: the module and attestation are published to all active producers with tracked completion in the portal.

checklist.step: Monitor completion progress against the due date

Send a targeted reminder and copy the individual's manager for those inside 5 days of the due date.
checklist.done: a weekly completion report drives targeted reminders, escalating to managers within 5 days of due date.

checklist.step: Restrict access or authority for anyone who lapses past the grace period

For employees, request suspension of AML platform/underwriting-system access from IT Security Manager until training completes.
For producers, request suspension of binding authority from the Producer Compliance Manager until training and attestation are complete.
Log the restriction, the date applied and the date lifted.
checklist.done: every lapse past the grace period results in a logged access or authority restriction, lifted only on completion.

checklist.step: Verify assessment scores meet the pass threshold before marking complete

Spot-check a sample of completions monthly to confirm the score/completion linkage is functioning.
Log any completion recorded without a passing score as a system exception.
checklist.done: completions verified to require an 80%+ score, with monthly spot-checks confirming the linkage.

checklist.step: Reconcile the employee roster to the LMS assignment list monthly
actions: Pull the current HRIS roster for in-scope roles and compare to the LMS assignment list.
Identify any employee in an in-scope role with no active assignment and assign immediately.
Identify any leaver still showing an active assignment and remove it.
checklist.done: the roster and LMS assignment list are reconciled monthly with gaps corrected same-month.

checklist.step: Reconcile the active producer list to the portal tracking log monthly
actions: Pull the current active producer list from the agency/producer management system.
Compare to the Broker & Agent Portal training tracking log.
Assign training immediately to any active producer missing from the tracking log.
checklist.done: the active producer list and portal tracking log are reconciled monthly with gaps corrected same-month.

checklist.step: File the annual completion report and attestations in the evidence repository
actions: Export the final Cornerstone LMS completion report and the producer attestation log at cycle close.
File both in the compliance evidence repository under the training cycle year.
Apply the 5-year retention label.
checklist.done: the completion report and attestation log are filed and retention-labelled for the cycle.

checklist.step: Report training completion rates to the Compliance Committee
actions: Compile the final completion rate for employees and producers, and the average assessment score.
Present to the Compliance Committee alongside any access-restriction actions taken.
Record committee direction in the minutes.
checklist.done: completion rates are reported to the Compliance Committee at cycle close with directions recorded.

checklist.step: Deliver targeted refresher training after any material incident or thematic finding
actions: Where a SAR quality issue, sanctions near-miss or FCA thematic finding points to a training gap, build a targeted refresher module.
Assign it to the affected population outside the normal annual cycle.
Track completion the same way as the annual cycle.
checklist.done: targeted refreshers are built and assigned promptly following any identified training-related gap.

checklist.step: Maintain role-based curriculum mapping
actions: Maintain a mapping of job role to required training modules (underwriting, claims, distribution, all-staff baseline).
Review the mapping annually against any new role created in the HRIS.
Update LMS assignment rules to match any mapping change.
checklist.done: the role-to-curriculum mapping is current and reflected in LMS assignment rules.

checklist.step: Audit LMS assignment-rule integrity
actions: Periodically test that a newly created in-scope role automatically receives the correct course assignment.
Confirm role changes (promotion, transfer) trigger reassignment where the new role has different requirements.
Log any rule failure to Learning & Development for correction.
checklist.done: LMS assignment-rule integrity is periodically tested with failures logged and corrected.

checklist.step: Confirm producer attestations are legally sufficient
actions: Review the attestation form wording annually to confirm it captures the producer's confirmation of training completion and understanding of reporting obligations.
Confirm the portal retains a timestamped, non-editable record of each attestation.
Update the wording where regulatory guidance changes.
checklist.done: the attestation form is confirmed legally sufficient and timestamped attestations are retained non-editable.

testing.step: Build the population of employees and producers required to train in the period
actions: Extract the full LMS assignment list and the Broker & Agent Portal tracking log for the cycle.
Reconcile both against the HRIS roster and the active producer list respectively.
Resolve any count difference before sampling.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to the roster and producer list and signed complete.

testing.step: Compute the completion rate and identify all shortfalls
actions: Calculate completion rate as completions with a passing score divided by the population.
List every individual not complete by due date plus the 10-business-day grace period as an automatic exception.
testing.done: the completion rate is computed and every shortfall is listed as an exception.

testing.step: Select and document the test sample
actions: Take 100% of individuals whose access/authority was restricted for non-completion.
Take a random sample of 10% of completed records, minimum 25.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and covers all restriction cases.

testing.step: Verify assessment scores behind sampled completions
actions: Pull the recorded assessment score for each sampled completion directly from Cornerstone LMS.
Confirm the score is at or above the 80% pass mark.
Log any completion below threshold as an exception.
testing.done: every sampled completion's score is verified at or above threshold, or logged as an exception.

testing.step: Confirm restrictions were applied and lifted correctly for the sample
actions: For each sampled restriction case, confirm the restriction date matches 10 business days past due date.
Confirm the restriction was lifted only after a verified passing completion.
Log any early lift or unapplied restriction as an exception.
testing.done: sampled restrictions are confirmed correctly applied and lifted, or exceptions are logged.

testing.step: Re-check role-to-curriculum mapping accuracy on the sample
actions: For each sampled individual, confirm the assigned course matches their current job role per the mapping.
Flag anyone assigned the wrong module for their role.
Log mismatches as exceptions.
testing.done: sampled assignments match the role-to-curriculum mapping, or mismatches are logged.

testing.step: Verify producer attestation integrity on the sample
actions: Pull the timestamped attestation record for each sampled producer.
Confirm the attestation cannot be edited post-submission and pre-dates any binding activity in the period.
Log any missing or editable attestation as an exception.
testing.done: sampled producer attestations are confirmed timestamped and non-editable, or exceptions are logged.

testing.step: Confirm new-joiner onboarding training met the 30-day deadline
actions: Pull all new joiners in the period from the HRIS.
Confirm onboarding training completed within 30 days of start date for each.
Log any late or missing onboarding completion as an exception.
testing.done: every new joiner's onboarding training is confirmed within 30 days, or exceptions are logged.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with the individual (role-level, not named, in the aggregate report) and what was missed.
Assign root cause and owner, and set a remediation date.
For any individual who transacted in-scope business while past due and unrestricted, escalate to Chief Risk Officer.
Carry open exceptions into the next cycle's test as mandatory retest rows.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the final completion rate against the 100%-by-grace-period threshold.
Write the conclusion referencing the evidence reviewed.
Have the independent Internal Auditor, outside L&D and AML, sign the workpaper.
Report results to the Compliance Committee and file the workpaper in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion is filed and reported to the Compliance Committee.
